result.summary: This unit is the contrib, examples, test and doc trees of the zlib 1.3.1 tarball: blast, puff, infback9, minizip, the iostream wrappers, the gvmat64 assembly, and example and test programs. I checked them for network use, process execution, environment or secret access, load-time constructors, hooking, encoded payloads and hidden switches, and found none. The code matches upstream zlib, and the non-source files are upstream docs and fixtures that nothing reads or compiles.

findings.title: Binary and unreadable files are upstream docs and fixtures
findings.detail: The .cs files under contrib/dotzlib/DotZLib, plus DotZLib.chm, contrib/blast/test.pk (8 bytes, matching the 'AIAIAI' example stream documented in blast.c), contrib/puff/zeros.raw and doc/crc-doc.1.0.pdf, could not be shown as source. All are standard files of the upstream zlib 1.3.1 distribution: documentation, test fixtures and C# bindings. None is marked as absent from the source repository. Nothing in the reviewed C sources reads, unpacks or compiles them, and a Zig/C build of zlib does not compile C# or use these fixtures.

findings.title: Assembly longest_match matches upstream contrib
findings.detail: gvmat64.S is the well-known longest_match optimisation by Gilles Vollant. It only reads deflate_state fields, compares window bytes and returns a match length. It makes no system calls, has no hidden symbols and does no self-modification. Its dsXxx struct offsets are hard-coded and would be wrong for current zlib, but it is not part of a normal zlib build.

findings.title: Example and test programs do only local file I/O
findings.detail: miniunz.c, untgz.c, gun.c, gzappend.c, gzlog.c, minigzip.c and the other programs are stock zlib example and test tools. They read and write files named on their own command lines. untgz extracts tar entries without path-traversal checks, a long-known upstream weakness. These are standalone programs with their own main() functions and are not linked into the library.
